problem:
If $A={p,q}$ and $B={2,4,6},$ which of the following elements belong to $A\times A\times B?$

- $(p,q,2)$
- $((p,p),4)$
- $(q,q,6)$

examples.problem:
If $A = \{ p,q \}$ and $B = \{ 4,9 \},$ which of the following elements belong to $(A \times B) \times B?$

- $((p,4),9)$

- $((q,9),4)$

- $(p,4,9)$
examples.worked_solution:
The Cartesian product $A \times B$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $A$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $B.$

In this case, $A \times B$ consists of every combination of $\{ p,q \}$ with $\{ 4,9 \},$ as shown in the schematic below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072443/assets/69ff8391a11b7bfa221b6b303f31551288bd969bdeed778fb05d3b7094e027ae.png)

Hence, the set $A \times B$ is given by

$$
A \times B = \{ (p,4), (p,9), (q,4), (q,9)\}.
$$

Note that 

$$
|A \times B| = |A| \cdot |B| = 2 \cdot 2 = 4.
$$

Now, the Cartesian product

$$
(A \times B) \times B
$$

consists of every combination of $A \times B$ and $B,$ as shown in the schematic below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072443/assets/5f4a74a98f9df15273d59131eadc1155ff2d1105e1027e7d10b7e2366102e046.png)

Note that 

$$
|(A \times B) \times B| = |A \times B| \cdot |B| = 4 \cdot 2 = 8.
$$

From the given options, we see that both $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}((p, 4), 9)}$ and $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}((q,9),4)}$ are in $(A \times B) \times B.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."

feedback.problem: What is the cardinality of $K\times M$ for $K={0,3,4,11,15}$ and $M={d,e,f}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
For any two finite sets $K$ and $M,$ the cardinality of $K\times M$ is

$$
|K\times M|=|K|\cdot |M|.
$$

In this case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|K\times M| & =|K|\cdot |M| \\  & =5\cdot 3 \\  & =15.\end{aligned}
$$
